note: The 'juan' agricultural series (rye/wheat/oats/barley/potatoes, ha & tonnes, 1922-1945) shows a smooth, roughly parallel ~20-30% decline across all five staples from 1939 through 1940-1944 (plateau-level wartime disruption, not a stepped territorial cut), followed by a sharp 1945 collapse (rye area -92% y/y) coinciding with the front line crossing the country Jan-May 1945 -- consistent with pre-war-territory reporting continuing through the occupation years rather than a documented switch to a reduced/zone-specific reporting basis, though the true wartime reporting convention (whole pre-war Poland vs. General-Government-only) could not be independently confirmed and remains an open question worth flagging on this page.

Checked juan-source Finland sown-area series (barley/oats/wheat, ha) for 1941-1960: values are smooth and continuous across 1941-1944 (Continuation War) and the 1944 armistice, with no step corresponding to the temporary Karelia recapture -- this directly resolves open question oq-continuation-war-territory for at least this source: it reports consistently on the post-1940 reduced-territory basis, not on the briefly-expanded wartime borders.

IIA source data labeled 'Russian Federation'/'Russia' for 1922-1940 is confirmed (via implausibly large cotton lint/cotton seed area for RSFSR-proper) to actually report whole-USSR territory, consistent with this row's documented RSFSR-to-USSR scope; this is a useful confirmed source-labeling convention for IIA-era Soviet data.

Confirmed against source "juan" (rows=603, years 1950-1960, iso deu, single undifferentiated "germany" label, no FRG/GDR split) -- exactly the failure mode the wiki's "Why this entry exists" section describes; this is direct corroborating evidence the DEU-1949-1990 aggregate-Germany design is correct for this source.

FAO 1952 yearbook 'Yugoslavia' series for population (r_fao_population_1952_10_18) reports a median ~5.08M for 1937-1947, roughly one-third of Yugoslavia's actual total population (~14-16M per 1931/1948 censuses); this FAO population figure likely reflects agricultural/rural population rather than total population and should not be read as evidence of a territorial mismatch -- other staple magnitudes (poultry, draft animals, crop areas) are consistent with full pre-1947 Kingdom of Yugoslavia territory.

Verified: 432 IIA rows labeled 'south korea' (iso=KOR) spanning years 1909-1945 route correctly to KOR-1800-1945 under the page's existing routing rule; this is a separate, larger, dated (non-null-year) batch from the 71 null-year rows already documented under iia-null-year-rows, and it independently corroborates that the IIA used 'south korea' as an anachronistic label for the whole peninsula prior to 1945.
